decision: plain droplet release on an app window keeps the highlight and opens the composer with a window context row
why: a drop should turn the window under the pointer into the task's target without a separate lock step

decision: submit captures the window first, then creates the task, and returns to editing when capture fails
why: the task needs the screenshot path in its prompt; a failed capture must not discard the typed task

decision: drop capture prompts label the context as a window, lock keeps its own label
why: the agent prompt should say what the screenshot is, and the persistent lock flow should stay distinguishable

decision: Option-drag cancel tests the island footprint instead of the panel frame
why: the drop panel now fills the desktop, so its frame can no longer identify the island

decision: the drop panel spans the union of every display
why: app windows live on the external display; a notch-screen-only canvas left the droplet stuck at x=0

decision: the drop anchor is converted from screen coordinates against the live window frame
why: the panel moves and resizes while the island stays fixed, so a captured local anchor would drift

decision: droplet rest, composer drop point, and lock badge follow the anchor, not the panel midpoint
why: the union panel is not centered on the notch
result: rendered fixtures match the old notch-centered layout

decision: only the droplet's old and new bounds are invalidated at 60 Hz
why: the union panel is 3648x1117 points; repainting all of it every tick is wasteful
result: builds green, not measured under a real drag

decision: opened a drop at launch through a temporary env hook to measure the live panel, then removed the hook
why: a synthetic drag is impossible without Accessibility permission, and the panel frame is the thing the union change must prove
result: union frame proven, hook removed before the release build

decision: accepted that the full-desktop drop panel swallows clicks outside the composer
why: AppKit cannot pass a click through a window; the alternative was a multi-window rewrite, and the composer is a modal quick-capture surface

decision: closing the drop composer stashes a non-empty draft and the next drop restores its text, kind, cwd, and worktree choice
why: an outside click or Esc should not destroy typed work, and the reviewer flagged that the old close discarded it silently

decision: the composer clamps to the display that contains the drop point, not the union rectangle
why: a drop near the seam could split the card across two displays

decision: final suite is 67 tests (2 skipped) and App-target views, drag coordination, and window capture still have no unit coverage
why: the earlier 24-test checkpoint only covered IslandCore and HerdrKit, and the fixtures are notch-centered

decision: kept the capture flow as is after review because the TCC prompt and ScreenCaptureKit call can block and the fix belongs in the capture service, not the drop reducer
why: the review flagged a hung capture locking the composer; changing it safely needs a timeout and permission-prompt redesign, which is a separate task

decision: submit success keeps the drop in a didCreate state for one exit motion before the overlay closes it
why: the reducer cleared the drop on success, so the panel snapped home and the designed 520 ms send-home return never played
result: full suite 67 executed, 2 skipped, 0 failures; updated drop submit test asserts the sent state and close handoff

decision: the droplet rest point now derives from the anchor instead of the panel midpoint
why: restPoint used bounds.midX, so on a union panel the droplet rested at the desktop center while the card and badge followed the anchor
result: external-anchor render shows the droplet, card, and ghost bar aligned at x=1000 on a 1400 wide canvas

decision: the composer reports its rendered height and the placement and NSView hit rectangle share that number
why: the height was hand-summed and the NSView dismissed clicks below any content drift; the card now sizes itself and is measured
result: build green, drop-external render shows the full window card at its intrinsic height

decision: corrected the click-through claim: AppKit can pass clicks through with ignoresMouseEvents, but the drop panel must still accept the droplet and the card
why: the panel already flips mouse policy for the ambient lip; doing the same for a full-desktop drop needs a card-frame plumb and a global monitor, deferred as a deliberate modal tradeoff

decision: one NSWindow still spans displays with different backing scales
why: the union panel frame is proven, but per-screen backing scale and Retina sharpness were not measured; a per-screen window design would be needed to guarantee both
result: open, not changed in this pass

decision: blocked and completion cues are reducer intent; the app resolves the per-event system sound at play time
why: the reducer already owns exactly-once attention bookkeeping across facts and snapshots, and the sound choice must not gate episode recording
